The Viterbi Family Department of Ophthalmology and Shiley Eye Institute at the University of California San Diego (UC San Diego) is an internationally recognized leader in patient care, education, and vision research. The department comprises 45 faculty physicians and scientists, 16 resident physicians, 13 postdoctoral clinical and research fellows, and more than 200 staff members across seven clinical divisions: Glaucoma, Retina, Cornea & Refractive Surgery, Pediatrics, Oculoplastic, Uveitis, and Neuro-Ophthalmology. Clinical services are delivered across multiple locations, including the Shiley Eye Institute, Ratner Eye Center, Perlman Medical Offices, Hamilton Glaucoma and Jacobs Retina Center, Hillcrest Eye Center, and the Veterans Affairs (VA) Medical Center. As the largest single outpatient clinic at UC San Diego, the department provides more than 130,000 patient visits and performs over 12,000 surgical procedures annually. The department continues to experience significant growth and is expanding its clinical footprint through development of the Shiley Eye Institute and regional satellite locations, including strategic practice acquisitions. Complementing its exceptional clinical enterprise, the department is a nationally recognized research center conducting innovative basic, translational, and clinical research on eye diseases. With more than $12 million in annual federal research funding from the National Institutes of Health, the National Eye Institute, and other sponsors, the department ranks among the nation's leading ophthalmology programs in federally funded vision research.

The incumbent is responsible for the strategic leadership, coordination, development, implementation, and oversight of the Department of Ophthalmology's administrative and financial operations in support of its clinical, research, and educational missions. The position oversees an annual operating budget exceeding $50 million in revenue and expense and serves as a key strategic partner to the Department Chair and Administrative Vice Chair in advancing departmental priorities, operational excellence, and long-term strategic initiatives. The incumbent provides executive leadership for the department's administrative infrastructure, including finance, research administration, human resources, academic affairs, faculty affairs, facilities, operational planning, and administrative services, while ensuring compliance with University, School of Medicine, and sponsor policies.

The incumbent oversees all departmental financial operations, including annual operating and research budgets, long-range financial planning, resource allocation, expenditure management, financial reporting, and complex financial analyses that support executive decision-making. Responsibilities include oversight of professional funds flow, clinical revenue allocations, staff salary administration, faculty compensation and incentive plans, and financial strategy development. The incumbent also provides strategic leadership for the department's research finance enterprise, overseeing a sponsored research portfolio exceeding $12 million and directing research administration, post-award management, budgeting, financial analysis, compliance, and reporting to ensure sound stewardship of departmental resources.

In partnership with the Department Chair and Administrative Vice Chair, the incumbent provides executive oversight of departmental administration through leadership of professional managers responsible for human resources, academic personnel and faculty affairs, facilities and space planning, staff and faculty relations, operational services, and organizational development. The incumbent collaborates with Division Chiefs and faculty leaders to support faculty recruitment, academic personnel actions, workforce planning, clinical program development, research growth, and operational improvements that advance the department's strategic objectives while fostering an inclusive, collaborative, and high-performing organizational culture.Working with broad organizational objectives, the incumbent independently establishes priorities, allocates resources, develops policies and procedures, and directs multiple functional areas through subordinate managers.

The position is accountable for achieving strategic, financial, operational, and compliance objectives while exercising a high degree of independent judgment in resolving complex organizational, personnel, and financial issues. Decisions made by the incumbent have significant impact on departmental performance, requiring exceptional leadership, analytical expertise, and accountability. The incumbent promotes continuous process improvement, staff development, succession planning, and operational excellence to ensure the Department of Ophthalmology remains well positioned to achieve its evolving clinical, research, and educational mission.
